title: Building on three clouds, and the ecosystem
dek: Terraform's open seams are the plugin protocol and the providers, and almost everything outside the core binary now runs out of process. This part reads the licence and the fork from their trees, measures the two one-way doors between Terraform v1.17.0 and OpenTofu v1.13.2, follows Stacks and Policy into downloaded and exec'd plugins, then builds one project on AWS, GCP and Azure and takes it through validate, 7 mocked tests and a 36-resource plan with no cloud credentials at all: where the database password goes, which provider refuses to plan, what mocks really fake, and why local policy is not enforcement. It ends with the collection's register of 101 findings.
byline: 24 October 2026 · Subject: terraform@018a99c8 (v1.17.0) · Part 4 of 4 · Read from the source; measured on this machine with no cloud credentials
description: Terraform v1.17.0 in its ecosystem and on three clouds: the BUSL licence and what stayed MPL, OpenTofu v1.13.2 measured (provider for_each and state encryption as one-way doors), Stacks and Policy as out-of-process plugins, a multicloud AWS/GCP/Azure project planned and tested with no credentials, write-only database passwords end to end, mock providers, local policy failing open, and the 101-item findings register. Part 4 of Terraform, taken apart.
og_description: Part 4 of Terraform, taken apart. 1,988 BUSL files and 7 MPL ones, and the 7 are the protocol; OpenTofu state with provider for_each or encryption cannot go back to Terraform; Policy and Stacks run as separate plugins; a three-cloud project plans 36 creates and 1 action with fake credentials, its database passwords never reach a file, google makes one real HTTPS call, azurerm needs a fake az, and local plan -policies fails open with exit 0.
twitter_description: The licence, the fork, the commercial plugins, and one AWS + GCP + Azure project planned and tested with no cloud credentials on Terraform v1.17.0. Part 4 of Terraform, taken apart, with the 101-item findings register.
